entities.summary:
Dermatology is the medical specialty devoted to the skin, hair, nails, and related mucosal surfaces—their structure, functions, and diseases. Although skin ailments appear in ancient medical texts, dermatology crystallised as a distinct modern specialty in the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries with hospital clinics, classification of eruptions, and later histopathology and microbiology.

Industrialisation, urban crowding, and colonial tropical medicine pushed skin disease into public-health view, while venereology often overlapped institutional boundaries. Twentieth-century dermatology added surgery, immunology, cosmetics, and oncology (melanoma), becoming both a high-tech and high-demand clinical field.

Today dermatology mediates visible health, stigma, and aesthetic culture—an essential specialty at the boundary of medicine and society’s surface.
